text:
# SEO and GEO audit for Trailhead

I read all 9 tracked files. The site is a small Nuxt 4 app with 3 pages. Problems are listed by severity.

## Critical

1. **The site is a client-rendered SPA.** `nuxt.config.ts:2` sets `ssr: false`.
   - The server sends an empty shell. Google can render JS, but slowly and unreliably.
   - Most AI crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot and similar) don't run JS. They see no headings, text or links, so there is nothing to cite.
   - **Fix:** remove `ssr: false`. For a mostly static site, use `nitro: { prerender: { routes: ['/', '/guides'] } }` or `routeRules: { '/**': { prerender: true } }`.

2. **`/guides` is blocked from indexing but listed in the sitemap.**
   - `server/middleware/headers.ts:2-4` sends `X-Robots-Tag: noindex` for every path starting with `/guides`. That is your main content section, and it would also match future `/guides/<slug>` pages.
   - `public/sitemap.xml:4` lists `/guides`. A noindex page in a sitemap is a contradiction that Search Console flags.
   - **Fix:** delete the middleware, or restrict it to `/admin`. If `/guides` was meant to stay private, remove it from the sitemap.

3. **The homepage doesn't link to the guides with a crawlable link.** `pages/index.vue:8` uses `<button @click="router.push('/guides')">`.
   - Crawlers don't click buttons, so there is no `<a href>` pointing to `/guides`.
   - **Fix:** use `<NuxtLink to="/guides">Trail guides</NuxtLink>`. Remove the unused `useRouter` at line 2.

## High

4. **The same title and description appear on every page.**
   - `app.vue:2` sets one title, `Trailhead`, which has no keywords and no per-page variation.
   - `nuxt.config.ts:6` sets one global description.
   - `pages/index.vue` and `pages/guides.vue` call neither `useHead` nor `useSeoMeta`.
   - **Fix:** add `useSeoMeta({ title, description })` in each page, for example "Peak District walks and trail guides | Trailhead". Set a `titleTemplate` in `app.vue`.

5. **There is no canonical URL, Open Graph or Twitter metadata.** The `head` block in `nuxt.config.ts:4-7` has none of these.
   - **Fix:** add `<link rel="canonical">`, `og:title`, `og:description`, `og:image`, `og:url`, `og:type` and `twitter:card`. Also add a favicon.

6. **There is no structured data.** No JSON-LD exists anywhere.
   - AI engines and Google use it to identify entities.
   - **Fix:** add `WebSite` and `Organization` JSON-LD in `app.vue` via `useHead({ script: [{ type: 'application/ld+json', ... }] })`. On guide pages, add `Article` or `ItemList`, plus `BreadcrumbList`.

7. **The content is too thin to rank or be cited.** `pages/guides.vue:3-4` has one H1 and one sentence. `pages/index.vue:7` has an H1 and a button.
   - There are no trail names, distances, grades, maps, dates or authorship.
   - **Fix:** add real content, ideally one page per route (`pages/guides/[slug].vue`). Write in answer-first, quotable form (distance, time, difficulty, start point) with a visible "last updated" date and an author.

## Medium

8. **`public/robots.txt:4` uses a relative sitemap URL.** The spec requires an absolute URL.
   - **Fix:** `Sitemap: https://trailhead.example/sitemap.xml`, using your real domain.

9. **`robots.txt:2` and `pages/admin.vue:2` conflict.**
   - `Disallow: /admin` stops crawlers from fetching the page, so they never see its `noindex`. Blocked URLs can still be indexed if linked.
   - **Fix:** put real authentication on `/admin` and keep one mechanism. Ideally allow crawling and keep `noindex`, or just authenticate it.

10. **The sitemap is hand-written.** `public/sitemap.xml:3-4` uses a placeholder domain (`trailhead.example`), has no `<lastmod>`, and will go stale as guides are added.
    - **Fix:** use `@nuxtjs/sitemap`, or better, the `@nuxtjs/seo` bundle. It also handles robots, canonicals, OG tags and schema, and would cover items 4–6 and 8–10.

11. **There is no AI crawler policy and no `llms.txt`.** `robots.txt` doesn't mention GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended or OAI-SearchBot.
    - **Fix:** decide whether to allow them (usually yes for citation) and state it explicitly. Optionally add `public/llms.txt` summarising the site and linking the key guides.

## Fix order

1. Fix items 1, 2 and 3 (SSR or prerender, the noindex header, the `NuxtLink`). Nothing else matters until crawlers can see and index the pages.
2. Add per-page metadata and structured data (items 4–6).
3. Write the real content and per-trail pages (item 7).
4. Clean up robots.txt and the sitemap (items 8–11).

I haven't changed any files. I can apply the fixes for items 1–5, 8 and 9 now if you want.
